messages:
jordan (AE): Ana hit a weird one during the demo — stream delivered but client failed parsing midway. Client sent console logs, attaching below.

ana (client-dev): Repro steps: start streaming summary, UI shows partial text then error: 'Unexpected token d in JSON at position 0'. Happens inconsistently (2/5 runs). Chrome 121 macOS and Safari iOS webview. No corporate proxy, demo from home wifi.

kevin (SE): Can you paste the exact SSE payload the client logged? Also is this Hosted trial or Dedicated POC?

ana (client-dev): Hosted trial. Console snippet:

```
EventSource message: \n
data: {"id":"m_1","delta":{"content":"First chunk\n"}}data: {"id":"m_2","delta":{"content":"Second chunk continues\n"}}\n\nUnexpected token d in JSON at position 0
```

kevin (SE): Hmm that shows two "data:" blocks concatenated without the blank line that terminates an SSE event. Browser's SSE parser expects a blank line between events. If two events are glued in the same TCP write and the intermediary doesn't respect flush boundaries, a partial termination can be missed. Could be proxy buffering/aggregation.

ravi (eng-oncall): digging. Pulling edge and runtime logs for those request ids... I see on our side we emitted two events back-to-back and the connector wrote them in a single net buffer: 

```
[2026-03-21T09:02:11Z] conn=0xabc stream start
[2026-03-21T09:02:12Z] sse: event: delta id=m_1
data: {"id":"m_1","delta":{"content":"First chunk\n"}}\n\n
[2026-03-21T09:02:12Z] sse: event: delta id=m_2
data: {"id":"m_2","delta":{"content":"Second chunk continues\n"}}\n\n
[2026-03-21T09:02:12Z] write: 2048 bytes (single syscall)
[2026-03-21T09:02:12Z] proxy: tcp coalesced by gateway buffer
```

kevin (SE): That "single syscall" + "proxy: tcp coalesced" is the smoking gun. Some proxies (cloud or ISP middleboxes) will re-chunk TCP frames and can remove the perceived event delimiter if the client reads mid-buffer. We should ensure we flush an explicit `\n\n` and call a flush syscall per event, or set headers that prevent buffering: `Cache-Control: no-transform`, `X-Accel-Buffering: no` for Nginx, and ensure Connection: keep-alive with small write size.

ana (client-dev): Short-term for demo — what's the easiest mitigation? I can try client-side tolerant parsing but that's messy.

ravi (eng-oncall): Short-term: i) enable SSE heartbeat/comments `:hb\n\n` every 8s to keep the connection alive and make event boundaries more visible; ii) force the runtime to flush after each event (we have a flag for per-event flush for debugging); iii) recommend the client add minimal reassembly logic: if JSON.parse fails, buffer the text and attempt to parse from the first `{` to matching `}` across subsequent messages.

kevin (SE): For production, we should avoid relying on client reassembly. We'll add a POC-specific runtime flag that does: per-event flush + `X-Accel-Buffering: no`. Also update runbook to advise customers on webview/proxy caveats.

jordan (AE): Ravi, can you flip the flag on org-ana-trial? We need to validate before tomorrow's live call. Also note the customer asked about pricing for Dedicated if this persists.

ravi (eng-oncall): Enabling per-event flush and heartbeat for org-ana-trial now. Note: this increases small write syscalls and may impact throughput for heavy concurrent POCs. Turning it on for single org should be fine.

infra-bot: feature-flag 'sse-per-event-flush-poc-ana' toggled ON for org-ana-trial by ravi

ravi (eng-oncall): Also opened infra ticket to add `X-Accel-Buffering: no` at our edge when streaming and to surface a header policy for customers behind corporate proxies.

kevin (SE): Client-side guidance to share with Ana's team: 1) avoid browser extensions that proxy content 2) use incognito for demos 3) implement small reassembly fallback for SSE messages that can occasionally be concatenated 4) exponential backoff for reconnects. I'll draft a 1-pager.

ana (client-dev): Thanks — testing now. I'll run 10 back-to-back demos and report.

jordan (AE): Good work. If tests pass we'll mark resolved for the next demo and follow up about Dedicated pricing and the edge-buffering note in the POC checklist.

ravi (eng-oncall): Monitoring logs for 10 runs. I see per-event writes now. Waiting on client confirmation.

infra-bot: monitoring alert stream: 10 checks pending for org-ana-trial

kevin (SE): Follow-ups: add short item in sales POC checklist: "enable sse-per-event-flush for flaky webviews" and add telemetry flag to detect concatenated-data incidents.

ana (client-dev): 10/10 runs succeeded with the flag on. No parse errors observed. Thanks everyone.

jordan (AE): Excellent. Leaving this thread open for the pricing + Dedicated ask, but demo-ready.
